texts.preamble: Mool Chand vs State on 16 November, 2019 Author: Sudhir Agarwal Bench: Sudhir Agarwal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad Court No. - 34 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 1932 of 1990 Revisionist :- Mool Chand Opposite Party :- State Counsel for Revisionist :- Rahul Bhardwaj, A. K. Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- A.G.A. Hon'ble Sudhir Agarwal,J. 1. 2. This criminal revision under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C., has been filed aggrieved by judgments and orders dated 04.01.1989 and 24.11.1990.
texts.facts: 2. This criminal revision under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C., has been filed aggrieved by judgments and orders dated 04.01.1989 and 24.11.1990. Thereagainst Revisionist has preferred Criminal Appeal No.7 of 1989 before Court of Special/Additional Sessions Judge, Mathura (hereinafter referred to as "Appellate Court") and Appellate Court while dismissing the appeal vide judgment and order dated 24.11.1990 has confirmed the judgment and order of conviction passed by Trial Court. It is contended that firstly prosecution has not proved that Revisionist was selling milk and secondly, there was no independent witness while collecting sample, hence, requirement of Section 10(7) of Act, 1954 was not complied and thirdly, Revisionist was below age of 18 years on the date of collecting sample, hence, it was incumbent upon Magistrate to comply with requirements of Section 20 AA of Act, 1954. 4.
texts.arguments: Here I am fortified by a decision of Madras High Court in Public Prosecutor Vs. Ramachandran, 1993(1) FAC 93. 8. Apex Court in State of U.P. Vs. Hanif, AIR 1992 SC 1121 said that there is no such law that the evidence of Food Inspector must necessarily need corroboration from independent witnesses. His evidence is to be tested on its own merits and if found acceptable the Court would be entitled to accept and rely on to prove prosecution case. Mool Chand vs State on 16 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73682305/ 3 9. Following the above authorities and taking similar view, this Court in Criminal Revision No. 976 of 1989 (Ramesh Chandra Vs. State of U.P.) decided on 11.12.2014 in para 18 of judgment said as under: "18. It is the duty of Food Inspector to call one or more independent persons to be present at the time of taking sample and once that is done by him it is sufficient but if the witnesses are not ready to come forward and sign the documents the Food Inspector cannot compel them and, therefore, where the attempt has been made but failed, lack of signature by independent witness would not vitiate the trial." Para 18 of judgment makes it clear and reads as under : "18.
